canonical_definition:
What it is. Across the surveyed work, ARC-Challenge is most commonly treated as the harder challenge split of the AI2 Reasoning Challenge, a multiple-choice science question answering benchmark built from scientific or grade-school exams and designed to be difficult for simple retrieval or word co-occurrence methods. Papers refer to it under several spellings, including ARC-Challenge, ARC-C, ARC-c, ARCC, and ARC_C, and usually contrast it with ARC-Easy. Descriptions vary slightly: some emphasize commonsense or scientific reasoning, some describe it as open-book QA, and another frames it as a closed-set reasoning dataset.

What it is claimed to measure. Across papers, ARC-Challenge is linked to 16 constructs and 14 behavioral indicators, so the reported measurement claims are spread across many targets rather than concentrated on a single one. The prevailing use is to measure commonsense reasoning and broader reasoning, with recurring claims that it also measures general ability, generalization, natural language understanding, and scientific reasoning. On the behavioral side, papers most often use it for multiple-choice question answering, language understanding task performance, question answering, scientific question answering, and zero-shot task performance.

Space of uses. Most papers position ARC-Challenge as one component of a broader benchmark suite rather than as a standalone instrument. It is frequently evaluated in zero-shot settings, though some work uses few-shot or chain-of-thought prompting, and papers also use it as a downstream or benign-performance check after interventions such as fine-tuning, unlearning, alignment, or compression. It is linked to 3 other instruments, most often lm-evaluation-harness, and also OLMES and OpenCompass.

Concerns raised. Concerns raised about ARC-Challenge focus on contamination. Papers use it to probe for contamination and report slight evidence of contamination in a tested model, and a smaller line of work considered it for a benchmark suite but did not include it because of contamination concerns.

characterization_sections.label: What it is.
characterization_sections.text: Across the surveyed work, ARC-Challenge is most commonly treated as the harder challenge split of the AI2 Reasoning Challenge, a multiple-choice science question answering benchmark built from scientific or grade-school exams and designed to be difficult for simple retrieval or word co-occurrence methods. Papers refer to it under several spellings, including ARC-Challenge, ARC-C, ARC-c, ARCC, and ARC_C, and usually contrast it with ARC-Easy. Descriptions vary slightly: some emphasize commonsense or scientific reasoning, some describe it as open-book QA, and another frames it as a closed-set reasoning dataset.

characterization_sections.label: What it is claimed to measure.
characterization_sections.text: Across papers, ARC-Challenge is linked to 16 constructs and 14 behavioral indicators, so the reported measurement claims are spread across many targets rather than concentrated on a single one. The prevailing use is to measure commonsense reasoning and broader reasoning, with recurring claims that it also measures general ability, generalization, natural language understanding, and scientific reasoning. On the behavioral side, papers most often use it for multiple-choice question answering, language understanding task performance, question answering, scientific question answering, and zero-shot task performance.

characterization_sections.label: Space of uses.
characterization_sections.text: Most papers position ARC-Challenge as one component of a broader benchmark suite rather than as a standalone instrument. It is frequently evaluated in zero-shot settings, though some work uses few-shot or chain-of-thought prompting, and papers also use it as a downstream or benign-performance check after interventions such as fine-tuning, unlearning, alignment, or compression. It is linked to 3 other instruments, most often lm-evaluation-harness, and also OLMES and OpenCompass.

characterization_sections.label: Concerns raised.
characterization_sections.text: Concerns raised about ARC-Challenge focus on contamination. Papers use it to probe for contamination and report slight evidence of contamination in a tested model, and a smaller line of work considered it for a benchmark suite but did not include it because of contamination concerns.
